analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 318-532 and 533-799). They are documentation only and contain no executable code, configuration or workflow. The patch excerpt shows the only change is a new v0.10.1 candidate header and rollout notes (head lines 11-138); it is truncated after a few bullets, so I could not read most of the added head text. I saw no changed code, so no regression is attributable to this PR from the supplied evidence.

The base excerpts describe previously shipped behavior that is relevant to the threat model:
- T-041: encrypted SSD prefix cache, including the debug-only DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE path, which the entry says is absent from release builds.
- Per-account scoping and the 30-minute sliding TTL.
- The SSD write cap and the larger restore staging for large-memory Macs.
- TB-011 and TB-003: App Attest handling, logout and credential revocation.
- The release pipeline, covering staging lanes, ad-hoc dev-branch signing and a relaxed installer signature check for pre-release versions only.

The changelog describes these, and the PR does not modify them. The visible v0.10.1 rollout text says logprobs stay disabled on specific models and that the coordinator must include a specific platform PR. Both are operational contracts outside the supplied evidence, so I record them as unverified rather than as findings. The patch excerpt also says page-cache accounting can count more memory as available. That is a runtime change, and its source is not in this batch.

A reviewer of the actual code diffs should check:
- the page-cache accounting change for memory admission or availability effects;
- the mlx-swift-lm pin bump from 7bed8216 to 6148b6da;
- GLM variable-frame-rate video handling and the logprob groundwork, including that it stays disabled.

No security conclusion in this batch depends on the unseen head text, so I do not request deeper review for these changelog units.
